questions.stem: The 'PANCHATANTRA' — a celebrated Sanskrit collection of animal fables used to teach statecraft and practical wisdom — was composed by which ancient scholar?

options.option_text: Valmiki, the Adi Kavi who composed Ramayana
Chanakya, the renowned minister-strategist
Vishnu Sharma, a Brahmin scholar and teacher
Vatsyayana, author of the Nyaya Sutras

questions.explanation: Vishnu Sharma composed the Panchatantra as a practical guide to niti (wise conduct) for the sons of King Amarashakti of Mahilaropya. Chanakya is frequently confused as the answer because both deal with statecraft, but Chanakya wrote the Arthashastra, not the Panchatantra. Vatsyayana actually authored the Kamasutra, not the Nyaya Sutras (Nyaya Sutras = Aksapada Gautama).

questions.stem: 'RAMCHARITMANAS' — Tulsidas's beloved retelling of the Ramayana that made the epic accessible to common people — was composed primarily in which language?

options.option_text: Sanskrit, the classical language of ancient India
Braj Bhasha, the medieval dialect of western UP
Avadhi, a dialect of eastern Hindi spoken in Awadh
Maithili, the language of Bihar's Mithila region

questions.explanation: Tulsidas wrote Ramcharitmanas (c. 1574 CE) in Avadhi, an eastern dialect of Hindi, specifically to make Rama's story accessible to non-Sanskrit-knowing devotees. Sanskrit was Valmiki's language for the original Ramayana. Braj Bhasha was used by Surdas in Sur Sagar. Maithili was Vidyapati's medium — a common exam trap since all three are medieval Hindi dialects.

questions.stem: 'INDICA' — the earliest surviving Greek account describing Mauryan India's administration, society, and geography — was authored by which visitor to the Pataliputra court?

options.option_text: Fa Hien, the Chinese Buddhist pilgrim and traveler
Ptolemy, the Greek geographer who mapped Asia
Strabo, the Greek historian of the Roman period
Megasthenes, Greek ambassador to Chandragupta Maurya

questions.explanation: Megasthenes was sent as ambassador by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya (c. 302 BCE); his 'Indica' is the primary Greek source on Mauryan India. Fa Hien is a frequent distractor — he was a Chinese pilgrim who came much later (~400 CE) and wrote 'Fo Guo Ji' (Record of Buddhist Kingdoms), not Indica. Ptolemy and Strabo never visited India.

questions.stem: 'KITAB-UL-HIND' — a comprehensive comparative study of Indian philosophy, mathematics, astronomy and customs written in Arabic — was authored by which medieval scholar?

options.option_text: Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan traveler who visited Delhi
Al-Beruni (Abu Rayhan Biruni), who accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni
Marco Polo, the Venetian explorer of Asian kingdoms
Amir Khusrau, the poet laureate of the Delhi Sultanate

questions.explanation: Al-Beruni (973–1048 CE), the Persian polymath, accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni's invasions and spent ~13 years learning Sanskrit to study India systematically. His 'Kitab-ul-Hind' is uniquely objective and comparative in approach. Ibn Battuta is the top distractor — he wrote 'Rihla' about his Delhi Sultanate visit under Muhammad bin Tughluq, a century after Al-Beruni.

questions.stem: The Sanskrit play 'MUDRARAKSHASA' — dramatizing the political intrigue by which the last Nanda king's minister was outmaneuvered to consolidate the Mauryan Empire — was written by which playwright?

options.option_text: Vishakhadatta, who depicted Chandragupta's rise to power
Bhasa, who wrote plays based on Mahabharata themes
Bhavabhuti, author of the play Uttararamacharita
Shudraka, the playwright of Mricchakatika (Little Clay Cart)

questions.explanation: Mudrarakshasa ('The Signet Ring of Rakshasa') was composed by Vishakhadatta (c. 4th–8th century CE). It depicts Chanakya's strategic use of Rakshasa's own signet ring to trap and eventually win him over to Chandragupta's cause. Shudraka's Mricchakatika is frequently confused as it is also a celebrated Sanskrit drama dealing with political themes, but covers an entirely different storyline.

questions.stem: 'RAJATARANGINI' by Kalhana is widely regarded as India's first systematic historical chronicle in the modern sense. Which of the following correctly identifies both the language of composition and the geographical scope of its history?

options.option_text: Pali language; chronicles the Mauryan Empire's expansion across India
Prakrit language; chronicles the Satavahana dynasty of the Deccan
Sanskrit language; chronicles the kings of Magadha kingdom in Bihar
Sanskrit language; chronicles the history of the kings of Kashmir

questions.explanation: Kalhana composed Rajatarangini ('River of Kings') in Sanskrit around 1148–1150 CE, covering the history of Kashmir from its mythological origins through the reign of King Jayasimha. It is notable for using dated sources, oral traditions, and inscriptions — hallmarks of historiography. Option C (Magadha/Bihar) is the most tempting trap since Pataliputra was the great historical centre, but Rajatarangini is exclusively Kashmir-centric.

questions.stem: Panini's 'ASHTADHYAYI' (c. 4th century BCE) is one of humanity's greatest intellectual achievements in linguistics. Which statement most precisely and correctly describes its content and scholarly significance?

options.option_text: An astronomical treatise that calculated planetary positions using Sanskrit numerals
A medical compendium describing surgical techniques and herbal remedies in detail
A grammar of Sanskrit in 3,959 sutras, regarded as the earliest generative grammar
A philosophical text reconciling Vedantic monism with Samkhya dualism in verse form

questions.explanation: Ashtadhyayi ('Eight Chapters') encodes Sanskrit grammar through 3,959 highly compressed sutras using a metalanguage of rules, meta-rules, and exceptions — a feat modern linguists recognise as the earliest generative grammar predating Chomsky by 2,500 years. Option A conflates it with Aryabhata's Aryabhatiya (astronomy). Option B conflates it with Charaka Samhita or Sushruta Samhita (medicine). Option D (Vedanta vs Samkhya) points to texts like Brahmasutra.
